utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik. Before you start, could you tell me how long are you going to take for your direct examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Well, I think about an hour and 15 minutes or perhaps an hour and a half, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I hope you could wind up your direct examination before the first break, which is about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Can you hear me? Can you hear the interpretation?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Once again, the same warning as yesterday, please, do not rush it and see that we do not speak over each other with our questions and answers. I hope you already got used to the Court environment.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I hope it will be all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yesterday, we broke off after Her Honour Judge Clark asked a question, I believe you grasped what was meant by that question but let me repeat it briefly. Did you personally see any plans or documents issued by the political leadership of the Bosniaks, Muslims, or their -- or the army or the military component, that is the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina? And if you did, where are these documents now? And one more question. Your documentation, that is the HDZ documentation, or the HZ HB, HR HB documentation, how was it catalogued? Where was it stored? And where should they be and who should be their owner? I believe that was the drift of your last question, Judge Clark. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I've understood that question. I did give it some thought, and I wish to tell the Honourable Court the following. We, from the political leadership of the Croat people of the Croat Democratic Union, Croat Community Herceg-Bosna, and later on Croat Republic of Herceg-Bosna, came by information and specific plans that the Muslim leadership and the so-called Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is Muslim armed forces, were getting ready for an attack, or as they put it, a liberate Mostar and turn south and come out on the coast. We had, and we have, documents of March, 1993, which demonstrate this, and I hope that this documentation is accessible to the Honourable Court. If not, we can submit it. Specifically, the Muslim top leadership at that time, from Sarajevo to the territory of Herzegovina, that is Konjic, Jablanica, Prozor and Mostar, transfers certain political and military leaders with a clear intent of conducting preparations as they put it for the struggle against the enemy forces, meaning by that the Croat Defence Council. There was, and there is documentation that Mr. Safet Cibo was transferred from Sarajevo, I repeat Sarajevo, which has absolutely nothing to do with the territory of Herzegovina, and immediately joined in the political and military activities in that area. To make it even more absurd, the Muslim leadership designated him the President of the War Presidency for three municipalities: Konjic, Jablanica and Prozor. Disregarding all the legal regulation that is were in force at the time. We also have in our possession documentation dating to August, 1993, when at a meeting in Zenica, the Muslim political and military leadership already specified, elaborated the well known plan Neretva 93. That plan explicitly speaks about the conquest of Mostar, Capljina and Stolac, and access to Neum, that is to the sea. Mr. Sefer Halilovic was preparing that plan directly with the consent of the front figure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Bender, in August, 1993, the HVO and what you describe as the so-called army of -- the Armija of Bosnia-Herzegovina was in conflict. They were at war. So, if you came by any documents on either side indicating plans to conquer or reconquer, that not really of interest to what we are talking about now. What you were discussing yesterday was before the conflict, in April and May of 1993, you had information, I believe, that the Armija had a plan to attack the HVO first. Now, you are giving us specifics that you weren't yet asked for, and you are avoiding the questions, answering the questions, which Mr. Krsnik put to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am sorry, but I think there is a slight misunderstanding. Mr. Bender, it is true, somewhat expanded on what was the subject of my examination, and I was talking about the developments in January, February, March or rather March and April, 1993, and we have already heard various testimonies about this and the arrival of Mr. Safet Cibo to the lands of Konjic, Jablanica, Prozor, and the beginning of the attack under his immediate leadership, because he was wartime president, but I wouldn't go into that because -- or else you might object to me that I was giving testimony. Mr. Bender spoke about this in this introduction but then he moved on to August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: At the moment, Mr. Krsnik, August is not really relevant because the parties were in -- I know you don't call it war, but certainly anybody else would call it war. What we are really talking about are the earlier plans, before the conflict erupted, between the previous allies, and also where these documents are and what was the arrangement when a document was produced, what happened to it? We've asked many times, but if the witness can't answer or won't answer, we will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: He can. Why not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bender, let us try to confine ourselves to April and May, 1993. I'm sorry, to March and April, 1993. And what is it that you know directly? Because the Court here always asks for one's personal knowledge and I appreciate that. Do you have any personal knowledge about the developments in Konjic, Jablanica, Prozor following the arrival of Mr. Safet Cibo, what happened, if you know, to the political and military leadership and the civilians in those lands, and if you have any documentation about that, where is it now?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said in my introductory part that in March and April, 1993, already that we had documents, that Mr. Cibo and his associates came to that area directly instructed to do so by the Muslim top leadership in Sarajevo. The --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Sorry, I have to interrupt you but do you have any concrete knowledge? What happened? I'm talking about a specific event. I may not ask you any leading questions, nor may I lead you in direct examination but do you have -- do you have anything that would testify to the attacks of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in those areas?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, already --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please slow down?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were open conflicts in the territory of Konjic and murder of Croats in the territory of the municipality of Konjic, and the most important thing is that the leadership, both in Konjic and Jablanica and Prozor was dismissed and Mr. Cibo was instead appointed president of the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know who was removed, who was the lawful leadership before he came?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know who it was exactly, but they were front men, they were locals from the lands of Konjic, Jablanica and Prozor, who could and did find some common solutions with Croats in those same lands.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge whether the Croat Democratic Union was allowed to continue with its activity in the territory of these three municipalities and do you know what happened to the HVO, or rather the civilians of Croat ethnicity in that area in March and April?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do. We in the political leadership were informed through our channels that some problems had occurred up there, that the HDZ and the HVO work had been prohibited and that camps had been set up for the members of the Croat Defence Council and the civilian population in those lands. I believe that the Honourable Court has some of this documentation. If not, this documentation is in the lands of Mostar and can be obtained, and one can also find witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to religious officials?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every religious official who did not sign, if I may put it that way, with the Muslims, suffered the same lot as the civilians. Specifically in Jablanica, I know that the residence of the priest was looted, that his car was driven away and that he had to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yesterday, you spoke about Dubrava. What month was it in that area called Dubrava -- no, first let me ask you. Is Dubrava near a locality called Rotimlje?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, tell me first, Dubrava, you told me Dubrava Plateau. Is it near a settlement called Rotimlje?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rotimlje is part of the Dubrava Plateau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Krsnik that we are not going to hear anything about how the documents are catalogued and archived. We have tried for half an hour and I take it we are just going to move on to something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right, right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Come, please, let's try to be specific. How was the documentation archived, how was it catalogued, where was it archived?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer -- I can only speak about the documentation in the territory of the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, for instance, where you were, in that place?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the relevant regulations which we took over from the former Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, we stored and archived our documentation in the lands of Mostar and neighbouring communities -- municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Bender, we can go into private session if you do not wish to speak about that in an open session, if you do not wish to indicate the place, the building, where was the archive?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need to say that I'd rather not specify the site of the archive because, of course, there are some military documents and so on and so forth, but if need be, one can enter into possession.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, I'd rather to leave the documentation, especially the military documentation, because there are confidential things and it's not really all right to disclose it, but if the Honourable Court wishes to go there, there is a lawful way to gain access to that documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, this is what we are trying to find out, Mr. Bender, because the Prosecutor has documentation which says that -- which he says is the HVO documentation, and these are, by and large, military documents, and they are in Zagreb. However, we haven't been able to establish the route to Zagreb, the way to Zagreb. We discuss the authenticity of every document. We challenge their authenticity and it will of great help to the defence, unfortunately, I did not discuss that particular matter with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, shall we go to the private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Perhaps we should clarify matters a little. Tell us, in how many places in Herzegovina in 1993, that is prior to the Washington Agreement, were the seats of power of the HZ HB, that is HR HB?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of the overall wartime situation in the lands of the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna, different institutions of the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna had their seats in different places. Specifically, the legislature had its seat in Mostar. The executive was in part in Mostar and in part in Grude, and the military power was distributed in several municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And was that the situation throughout 1993? Were these bodies, did these bodies have their seat in Mostar during 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the legislature was in Mostar all the time, and the executive power was in part in Mostar and in part in Grude.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I've asked you all this because I was prompted by Her Honour but also because I have problems to gain access to the archives of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and as for the other documents, I have the same access to the Zagreb archives as my learned friends. These are our only sources. Now the archive of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, is it also the property of the federation?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The archive of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that is Muslim armed forces and the Croat Defence Council, is likewise the property of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina -- and Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You see, I wrote on various occasions to the President, to the Prime Minister, to the Presidency of the federation. Some allowed me to get to those documents. Others, however refused access. I have, for instance, a decision of President Krizanovic, that I must be allowed access to the archive of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina but deputy minister, and I do not know his name but I have the documentation to that effect, told me that he could not meet my request. And that is why I'm asking you, which authorities are in charge of this? Because you were in politics for a long time, and that is why I'm asking you, so that not only I, but the Honourable Court could also approach these authorities, and who is obeying whom?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, things that have been happening for the past year, year and a half, are not something that I know about, but I'm surprised that members of the Presidency are not treated with due respect. It was different in my time. After I was removed from the list for reasons that I have explained, a member of the Presidency, any of them, if he issued an order, it had to be executed wherever -- anywhere, any place in the territory of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I believe the Honourable Court needs to intercede with the President of the Presidency - at present, it is Mr. Belkic - and ensure both for the Court and for the Defence, access to the documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, we shall do that. I mean the Defence will do it. And my last question in this regard, even though Their Honours may have some questions later on, but we -- I see documents here which the Prosecutor is proposing, and the Prosecutor says that they received these documents from the authorities of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and this is correspondence dating back three or four years back, now which are the sources? Are these the authorities of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina or the authorities of the federation? And do the authorities of the federation have the right to call themselves the authorities of the republic?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such claims come as a surprise to me because after the Dayton Accords, there has not been, nor there may exist, the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna or the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And therefore, the agencies of these institutions, all the powers had been transferred to the authorities of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me, please, when the Prosecutor writes the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, who is that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, after all, I am a protagonist of a legislative body and I must say that there is no such body as the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. There is the council of ministers of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which discharges certain duties in accordance with the Dayton Accords. I'm not aware, nor is there, the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honour, we have just received a list with documents and it says -- might as well do it later on. I don't want to do it with this witness. I do not think we want any further discussion with him but I will seek clarification from our learned friends later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I was just trying to warn you when you were talking to Mr. Meek your microphone was on, and I could hear you and I think everyone else could.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour, but I have nothing to hide.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Bender, let us try to move on to another subject. There are two or three more topics, those that I thought we should cover. We have another hour at our disposal. Will you please be so kind as to tell me whether you personally have any knowledge, or whether you are taking part -- or whether you took part in the Geneva talks, in the drafting of the Vance-Owen Plan, if yes, what do you know about that? And finally, do you have any personal knowledge whether -- about the implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan, the meeting in Medjugorje on the 18th of May, 1993? What do you know about these things? I know that these are two or three topics that I put together but they are all interrelated.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, I did not take part in the talks in Geneva, but our representatives briefed the relevant agencies of the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna about the course of these negotiations, and the Vance-Owen Plan. The relevant authorities of the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna accepted the Vance-Owen Plan and were ready to enforce it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Just a small side question: Did you discuss the implementation with the SDA? Did you agree on the governors? Can you tell us something about that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is what I was about to say. The Croat Community Herceg-Bosna, we in the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna discussed and proposed the leaders of the provinces. However, at the other side did not do that so the plan could not be implemented. In other words, the Muslim side did not designate the front men for the provinces, and that is why the Vance-Owen Plan could not be translated into life.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm going to have to object at this point on the level again of generality we are talking about. We are just simply not getting any information whatsoever about what this man did, who he met with, which Muslim officials, SDA officials did he meet with, which SDA officials refused to implement the plan, which HDZ officials nominated people to be members of the so-called "cantonal governments," we are talking in just absolute complete generalities, which is, I submit, not very helpful to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik, you have to caution the witness about the specificality on these issues. We want exact information concerning all the matters mentioned in his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour. Sometimes I try -- I curtail the witness in his answers, sometimes I let him go on, and I think that he would have said all that himself without the intervention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So can you be more specific what meetings with the SDA, who was the leader of the SDA, who participated in the negotiations, who refused to sign? Your personal knowledge about all this.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that I did not participate in the talks in Geneva, but our bodies, headed by Mr. Boban, who was our president, Mr. Mate Boban, so he came to several places, he came to our Medjugorje, and they carried out negotiations with the representatives of the Muslim side, that is the Party of Democratic Action, headed by Mr. Izetbegovic, and if the Croatian party -- Croatian side accepted, then -- and the other didn't, then it is clear who the other party is and why the -- why this wasn't carried through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: It may be clear to you but it is not clear to us, it is not clear to the Honourable Court. We did not live there at the time in that area, and I always say to my witnesses, we were not there, even us in Zagreb found it very difficult to understand some things, let alone the Honourable Judges, who have now been faced with this for the first time. That is why it is very important for to you say everything you know.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will be very specific. The Presidency of the Croatian Community Herceg-Bosna, i.e. our president, the late Mate Boban, signed the Vance-Owen Plan, appointed the governors of the provinces, the Muslim side, headed by Alija Izetbegovic, didn't do that. And that is why the Vance-Owen Plan was not enforced. Why did the Muslim part not do this? It is -- they should be asked that. We believed that they did not want a peaceful solution but that they rather wanted to deal with the matters by war, which I have already said when answering your other questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Before we move on to the Owen-Stoltenberg plan, the witness in this courtroom --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, I was just checking whether -- can we move on to private session? I don't want to make a mistake. I just want to verify a fact, whether my learned colleague maybe can help me, whether a specific witness was in an open or a closed session. Neither Mr. Meek nor myself are sure about that. And we don't want to make a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik [Microphone not activated] I'm a little bit hesitant to say what we hear from the testimony of this witness is not the firsthand knowledge. I really don't know how far you could go in this direction. We have heard the testimony of other witnesses on this issue many times. We know what position you hold on the Defence part. Of course, we also know the position on the Prosecution's side. I wonder whether you would like to pursue this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is not really as simple as that. This gentleman has a personal knowledge and although he may not have been present when things were signed, he actually was present during the implementation or non-implementation of this plan and was where he has personal knowledge. This is not a period which lasted for a week. The international plan started in 1992 and ended in 1993 with the Washington plan and this gentleman is one of the members of the legislative power which was supposed to enforce these plans, and obviously, he does have personal knowledge, although he may not have been in Geneva but he was the one who was supposed to implement or participate in the implementation of this plan. I can move on. I just wanted to ask the witness about something that a witness said in this courtroom, and I wasn't sure whether he said it in an open or a closed session. We already talked a lot about this witness. He said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Kljujic, in his testimony said that the Croats or the representatives of the Croatian people always had a pencil ready in their back pocket and they always ran out to sign whatever plan. Was he able to know that? Did he participate in any -- the first question is: When did Mr. Kljujic leave HDZ, your personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kljujic was the President of the Croatian Democratic Union from September, 1991, until February, 1992, and I was his first vice-president at the time. I know him very well, and if I have to, I can say a few things about that. At the time Mr. Kljujic was involved and after that period, he was not involved in our politics. Neither of the HDZ nor of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna because he resigned from all his offices and this was adopted and at our subsequent meeting, and he was dissolved of all his duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Before his resignation, what were his political views in 1991 and the beginning of 1992? What policies did he pursue? You were his first vice-president, his first --

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say that Mr. Kljujic was not a serious and not up to the positions that he held. He was -- he would say one thing and he would do another, i.e. he would do very little. Because he was nothing but a sports journalist. At the beginning of his work, as we say, he grovelled up to Mr. Tudjman and later on, he grovelled up to Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, and it is up to you to conclude whether this is credible behaviour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what were his political views on the organisation of Bosnia and Herzegovina? In 1991 and 1992?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the first to advocate the subdivision of Bosnia and Herzegovina. There are a number of documents corroborating that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was he removed by President Tudjman?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't make me laugh. President Tudjman could not remove Mr. Kljujic, because Mr. Kljujic was the President of the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Mr. Kljujic resigned. The resignation was accepted and we actually were the ones who dissolved -- relieved Mr. Ljujic of all his duties. So the central committee of the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I repeat, I was the first vice-president of the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, Mr. Kljujic said that Mr. Tudjman had sent Mr. Stipe Mesic to Siroki Brijeg to remove him, to dismiss him. Were you at that meeting in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was at the meeting in Siroki Brijeg. I participated in it actively. We adopted some decisions. Amongst other, Mr. Stipe Mesic was participating in the meeting. At the time he was the second figure of HDZ of Croatia and the second figure of -- in the Republic of Croatia but he was nothing but a guest. He could not make any decisions. Therefore, it is not -- what Mr. Kljujic said, what Mr. Stjepan Kljujic said is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did Mr. Kljujic end up in hospital after that meeting, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Mr. Kljujic, according to the information that we received, that he ended up in a hospital, but he attended that particular meeting when he attended the meeting, he had already been ill. That you could tell by his appearances and by his behaviour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So, why does he then -- said that the Croats were pursuing international representatives and were running out to sign international agreements?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kljujic is not a serious person, and not a responsible person, and this is not true. Whatever we signed, we carried through. When it comes to the provinces, I know that the province in the area of Herzegovina, for that province, Mr. Pero Markovic was appointed as its governor, and that he was getting ready to assume that post, and the same situation was in other provinces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you participate personally in the implementation of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Owen-Stoltenberg plan? And what was the difference between the Vance-Owen and the Vance-Owen-Stoltenberg plan?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I participated in the implementation as a member of the Presidency of the HDZ, and as a member of the Presidency of the Croatian Community Herceg-Bosna, and I didn't participate in the talks. According to the Owen-Stoltenberg plan, the union of three republics --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me, I have to ask you generally, do you know anything about who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that we, the Croats, signed it. We accepted it. And we were ready to enforce it to the end. As far as I know, the Serbs did not accept that, for reasons known to them, because they wanted to annex Bosnia and Herzegovina to Yugoslavia. I don't know what the situation was with the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, I'm just looking at Mr. Bender's summary, witness summary, and you don't seem to be really sticking to it. You're going outside it, and leaving other aspects alone. He wasn't scheduled to talk about the Vance-Owen Plan or any of the other proposed or effective peace plans. You have him talking about how people procured citizenship, how he was a member of a delegation on several times in the office of President Tudjman, and various other things that he's talked about, but aren't you going a little bit outside?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You are?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, you are right. As always I'm honest. That's the way God made me. After 11 months in this courtroom and conversations and presentations, allow me to forget sometimes what is in the summary. But some answers actually make me try and clarify some things, and I'm convinced that the Honourable Court will also be interested in hearing the positions, i.e. the views, i.e. the testimony, of Mr. Bender about the things in which he participated himself, just like Mr. Kljujic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You are of course right, Mr. Krsnik. We are interested. It's just that as you only have a certain amount of time, I notice there are some issues that you're going to have to back track on and just to remind you not to forget them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very briefly, I would ask you to give me the reasons for the foundation of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. When was that? And another question: I believe you are a learned person and you can follow my question. Were there any discrimination or segregation of Muslims, any dismissals from work or religious discrimination? And how long -- to what extent were Bosniaks and Muslims present in the HVO? Let's end with the HR HB and let's move on to what Her Honour has just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna was founded on 28 August, 1993. All the documents about the foundation of -- about the founding of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, I hope, are available to the Honourable Court. We formed all the relevant bodies. There was no segregation whatsoever in the area of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna and there was also no discrimination. In our bodies, state bodies, there were at the time members of the Muslim people. Our university, there were several Muslims, members of the faculty. There were professors who were also Serbs. In our schools, we had people -- representatives of all the three peoples working, and attending those schools. And there was no segregation on any grounds. For a while, for example, the university was located in Neum. It was moved to Neum. And everybody there enjoyed the same things as the population of Neum. So there were Muslims, Croats and Serbs there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Bender, I ask very open questions and that is the way I will behave as well, so if we present everything to the Honourable Court, we can reach the truth, whatever it may be, as I like to say, we've heard here that Muslims or Bosniaks who were dismissed, some people who testified here, or some others, that they were dismissed, that they were fired from their jobs because they were Muslims, for no other reasons but that. We also heard members of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Bregava Brigade, that is the area of Rotimlje and Dubrava, who testified before this Court that they were arrested for no reason, other reason, but for being Muslims. What can you say about that? Was indeed anybody dismissed or fired?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is simply not true. The only people -- people who lost jobs -- everybody lost their jobs because of the war, but it happened to the same degree to Croats, Muslims and Serbs. Muslims at the time, that is members of the Croatian Defence Council, together with Croats, but in the area that you've mentioned, Rotimlje and Dubrava, but that is the same thing, because Rotimlje is a parts of Dubrava. I always said that in July, 1993, Muslims who were members of the Croatian Defence Council killed 18 Croat -- Croatian soldiers with whom they had fought together before, and our military organs, the prosecution and the military courts, had to take some measures because we could not allow any further killings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you receive reports of the military court or the military prosecution, you, in the legislative body of the government?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received official reports and sometimes we even asked to receive some documents from the military court and the military prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you personally know whether there were any measures ordered by the military court, the detention and investigations and against how many people, if you know that personally?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, again I'm going to repeat the objection I made some minutes ago. This is entirely general. We are talking about throughout the territory, claimed, at any time by Herceg-Bosna, between any time in November, 1991 and sometime in 1994, 1995? Who? Where, when, how, names, places, dates? Could we have some help, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, if you want to pursue this issue, you have to ask specific questions, indicating the time frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. This is exactly what I know. I was moving towards that. I am referring all the time to 1993. I'm not at all concerned with 1994 and 1995, and I hope this is clear. I hoped this is clear to my learned friend. Whenever we are mentioning a here, that it is 1992, 1993. Let's just move on briefly and I believe that we will come to that documentation very soon, I hope. And I hope that the Honourable Court will help me with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What year were you referring to when you said that you received reports from the military court and the military prosecutor's office? What year did you refer to?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring to the years 1992, 1993, and these were exactly the years that we are talking about all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let's move on because the time is running short. Let's talk about important topics. Tell me, two questions I have. First, did the Republic of Croatia send its military units and controlled the conflict in Bosnia and Herzegovina? Your personal knowledge. So, the Croatian Army in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know that at the time I was one of the leading figures of the Croatian politics in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I gave you my position at the time, and I now claim in full responsibility that at the time, there were no organised units of the Croatian Army in Bosnia and Herzegovina. But there were individuals who at the beginning of the war went to Croatia. So, both Croats and Muslims from Bosnia and Herzegovina, when the situation became somewhat calmer in Croatia, they returned to Bosnia and Herzegovina to help their people, to defend their homes there. I know Mr. Praljak, Mr. Obradovic, and other non-commissioned officers, and soldiers, from Neum, Stolac, Mostar, Siroki Brijeg, Central Bosnia and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the Republic of Croatia, did it control all of you, including the conflict?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I must repeat, and I've already said that, that the Republic of Croatia could not, and it indeed did not control either us or the Croatian community or the Croatian Community Herceg-Bosna or the Croatian Democratic Union or the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina, because it simply couldn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is this the first time you are testifying in this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I came to the Tribunal was yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did anyone ever try to communicate with you from the Prosecutor's Office or investigators to ask you about what you knew about the developments in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, until now nobody ever communicated with me, nor did I make any statements, but I am willing, whenever necessary and wherever necessary to present my knowledge to present the truth, because it suits best the Croats in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let me ask you something specific. Neum, that is the Bosnian and Herzegovinian territory is it? Did the Croatian Army ever go through Neum?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right. Neum was and is the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Croatian Army did pass through Neum, especially at the time when it was getting ready to liberate Slano and Dubrovnik. But we discussed this activity with representatives of the Croatian state and Croatian Army, with the participation of the international representatives of the international community, and it was agreed, and the representatives of the international community were very well informed about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And they knew it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They knew it because they were together with us at all the meetings, and there are these -- there exist people and documents about that, because the Croatian Army took the highway through Neum and naturally, in the lands of the Republic of Croatia, it was getting ready to liberate those areas around Slano and towards Dubrovnik, and praise be to the Lord, it was done well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Bender, let us move towards our final topic. Did you attend some meeting in the offers of the president of the Republic of Croatia, Mr. Franjo Tudjman?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was personally present at several meetings which -- in the Office of the President of the Republic of Croatia, Mr. Franjo Tudjman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were those discussions recorded?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were not. We were not warned about anything like that, whether somebody did it without us knowing about it, I do not know that. But I'm not aware that these discussions were being recorded, nor had anyone warned us about the recording.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you get copies of the latest versions of the minutes or records of those meetings?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, and our relevant bodies, whose member I am, never received any minutes from those meetings held in the Office of the President of the Republic of Croatia, Mr. Franjo Tudjman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Why did you go to President Tudjman?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the Honourable Court, and you personally, are aware that the international community had bound with certain -- Tudjman, President Tudjman with certain obligations to represent the Croats from Bosnia-Herzegovina and we empowered him to do so, but at those our meetings, our representatives were always present. That is meetings at President Tudjman's, we went to receive information about his thoughts and knowledge, simply to -- so that he could inform us about what went on at the meetings that he was attending, and what was the international community proposing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'd like to ask our distinguished Madam Registrar to prepare for us records PP -- PT24, 27 -- 24, PT27, PT28, PT33 and 35.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honours, it has just occurred to me, I have a suggestion. I will finish within the 20 minutes but perhaps we could make the break until 4.00 so that Mr. Bender refreshes his memory, and then to finish within 20 minutes, and then after the presidential transcripts, I will perhaps have a couple of questions only about our client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think we will have our break until 4.00. We have 20 minutes' break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I am sorry, I'm thinking whether to tell you or not. Could the second break be a little longer because my colleagues have just told me that I was responsible for this short break and they hold it against me. Of course, I didn't do that, I didn't want to do it, it was not deliberate, but there was quite a critique of me --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Bender, I'll be very brief because I suspect, judging by the list that we received from the learned friends that the Prosecutor will ask you more questions about the transcript than I will, but what I'd like to know is if you've had time to leaf through them, did you see your name there? Did you see your name to show that you participated, that is that you intervened at some point?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time that I see these papers, the first time that I have them. I just leafed through them. Yes, my name does come up in these papers. But if you want me to be more specific, then we have to do it gradually and I need more time to go through it rather than just peruse it, but I can give you my general view about these papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, let's then start from the beginning and I won't deal with all of them. The 13th of February, 1994, do you have pages 6, then in brackets 8, then in brackets JG?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is PT 24, Your Honours. Could we have it in the ELMO? It is in the left corner can you see those numbers? No, no, no, this transcript. You have to open the page if you are to see these numbers in the upper left corner.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is nothing in the upper left corner. There is in the right corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, in the left corner you have very small numbers?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: 6, then 8 in brackets, JG. And the Prosecutor's number is RO, this is in the right-hand corner. RO 157467.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So here we have your name and on that page, and on page 6-9, that is the next one, it looks as if you were the one who said that. And will you then look at it? We have empty space, we move on to page 7-1. Somebody is speaking but it doesn't say who. Have you had a look?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. I see what this is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me first, are you the author of these words? Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, I just cast a look at this. What it says here is not my style, is not the way that I speak. And especially on this last page that you are talking, 7/1, that is this black number 469 in the end, which refers to the disintegration of Bosnia-Herzegovina, I did not speak about that, nor is this how I speak. It is -- so therefore this is not authentic because it does not -- this is not my manner of work or rather this is not how I speak. And I also think that this is not true, in so far as I could see during this short time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now will you take the next transcript, please? And that is 11th of June, 1994. PT27. Will you look for page 2 (1) (HLJ). Prosecutor's number RO 157802.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've found it. The document and the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: According to this transcript, your intervention is almost half -- one page -- one and a half page long.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a look at it, merely cursory. I think on page 803, the references to an interjection, and it says, "One got killed." The President of the Republic of Croatia, Mr. Tudjman, chaired those meetings. There were no interjections. And moreover, I never speak that long. I doubt that these are documents. This is not my style of work or speech.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you look at the next page, 2-3-HLJ, right, the next one, RO 157804? There, your intervention takes two and a half pages, almost three pages.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't had time to look at all of it, but I repeat, from these first sentences, from two or three of them, I cannot confirm that this is what I said. And my intervention never took more than a minute, perhaps two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let us move on now to the document of the 2nd of September, 1994, which is PT28. Oh, see I forgot to ask you: Were you present at those meetings on those dates, the first two we went through and this third one?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I should have been at those two first meetings, yes, I'm confirming that I was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And at this meeting on the 2nd of September, 1994, did you attend that one?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can remember, of course it was a long time, I don't remember that I was present at that meeting on the 2nd of September, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I apologise, I am also leafing through this to see if your name appears anywhere, whether you took the floor. Yes. But you see, on page 5-2-HLJ, Prosecutor's number RO 157968, you are speaking, and your intervention is three and a half pages long, and later on, you also have a few brief interventions.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall being present there but just to say yes or no, I'd have to read it, but I doubt that I would have been given the floor for such a long time at the president's -- at the president's of the Republic of Croatia, but if you want me to answer that, I'd like to ask you to give me some more time to have a proper look.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. Will you now look at the record of the 27th of March, 1995? It is PT33.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you are on the first page already and again your intervention takes two and a half full pages. And then you take the floor again. So tell us, were you at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Can I ask you, it may be a question of translation but I don't have the transcripts in front of me, but I will look at them when I go to my Chamber, are you saying contribution or intervention? You said on the first page, again your intervention takes two and a half full pages. And then you take the floor again. Do you mean, does it say intervention on the transcript or --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says, "discussion" so it will be contribution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The other one is -- I think you mean a contribution. Is that what you mean, a contribution?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I said on the first page, the word I used was "contribution," taking part in a discussion, that is what the word means, to take the floor. But Mr. Bender said that there was one interjection. So perhaps interruption is -- perhaps that was an interruption that somebody did it but he also said that that was not what usually happened during meetings in the Office of the President of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this meeting of the 27th of March, 1995, as far as I can remember, yes, I was present, but as I have already said with reference to the previous meetings, will apply to this one. I cannot confirm that, that this is authentic and I cannot say that I really took that long, but if you want some details, then we can go into them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I will now ask the Honourable Court -- I do not know how long my learned friends will take for their examination, but if you are not asked any questions about presidential transcripts today, perhaps these documents could be left with you overnight because I believe the Prosecutor will have a number of questions about them to ask you.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you want any details regarding these transcripts, then, can I have a proper look at them?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can give him my copy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, I mean this is the first time that I see all these pages and we really cannot go into all the details because I'm a very serious-minded person and I do not wish to talk without some ground in facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we are not -- the details of those documents. I think you have already asked all the questions concerning those -- the authenticity of those documents. And I have to remind you that your time is up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Five minutes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: My last two questions, and the last presidential transcript of the 24th of November, 1996, it is PT35. Did you attend that meeting?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: First we have to clear up, it is the November 1995 or 1996? Because what I have here has been corrected. If it is 1995, then I was not there, because I remember that I was at a friend's in Dubrovnik. And in 1996, I'd have to have a look at the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite right, Witness. Can we please have it on the ELMO? Because I do not know which year this is either. It has been corrected, you can see, Your Honours, for yourselves. And this is a correction by hand. Very well, since we do not know the date, I won't have any questions about this any more. And my last question, Mr. Bender, did you -- have you ever heard or seen personally or have you ever been told that Mr. Mladen Naletilic has ever been to see Mr. Mate Boban and attend meetings? First did you see him personally there or did anyone tell you about seeing him there?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, I never saw Mr. Mladen Naletilic in Mr. Boban's office or at our meetings. I did not hear it from those persons that I met and cooperated with. I did not hear it from them that the gentleman concerned had been in Mr. Mate Boban's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was he ever a member of a delegation and in that capacity was present in Mr. Mate Boban's office? For instance in the negotiations with the SDA?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of my presentation, I said that Mr. Mladen Naletilic was not a member of any body of the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna or the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna. He was not a member of the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and therefore, he could not be at those meetings and talks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did he have any high-ranking military post?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the offices that I held and commitments and duties that I had, had he occupied any high-ranking military post, I would have met him and talked with him, but I never saw the gentleman concerned. We simply did not happen to meet during those wartime years of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And my very last question: Was he a coordinator between the HZ HB and the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no coordinators between the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HDZ of the Republic of Croatia. Therefore, the gentleman concerned could not be one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Meek just warned me about a mistake in the transcript. I asked you whether he was a coordinator between the HZ HB, not the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HDZ of the Republic of Croatia. My question is whether he was a coordinator between the HZ HB and the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no coordinators between the HDZ and the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna and the Republic of Croatia and the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina. These -- such offices and such persons did not exist. Therefore, the gentleman concerned could not hold those offices that you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the Prosecutor who says that, not I. Thank you. Thank you for coming, and now I leave you to the Prosecutor. Your Honours, thank you for your patience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seric, any direct examination? Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Scott, I believe that you have the same amount of time as the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the usher's assistance, please, if the witness could be shown the map that's been marked Exhibit P1. And for ease of use, perhaps Mr. Usher you can fold that in such a way that we can see the coast of the Croatia in the area of Split and that vicinity. Mr. Usher, if you could put that on the ELMO in such a way, please, to show the area that I mentioned earlier, approximately the area showing the Croatian coast line generally around Split. I'm not really interested in Split but you might find that easier than some of the others. All right. Now, in that same general area, perhaps the witness can of course assist, find Neum on the map, please, and if we could centre that approximately, then, once we find it on the map? All right. I think for these purposes that's probably fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, we did not see it or we missed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm going to come back to it now. I think in general we have the map, Mr. President, I'm sorry, I think generally we have the map about oriented where we can see the locations that I'll ask the witness about. And Mr. President, for the Chamber's assistance, you can Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. see approximately on the right half of the page but a little above the centre of the page, I think you'll find Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, sir, if you have a pointer available to you can you please then point out to the Chamber again where Neum, the city of Neum is?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neum is in the area that I'm showing to you right now. The only outlet that Bosnia and Herzegovina has to the Adriatic Sea.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell the Judges, please, not -- I'm not asking you for a straight distance on the map, but in terms of the driving distance from Neum to Mostar, approximately what is that distance or what -- if it helps or is easier for you, the approximate driving time to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have made that journey several hundreds of times because I live in Neum, and I used to work and I still work in Mostar. Currently, it takes some -- about 70 minutes, a little bit over an hour. And during the war, it was different because you had to take a different route.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, please tell us how long it took during the war.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult to say how long it took, because, for a while, the Neretva valley was not passable, so we would go either via Citluk and Siroki Brijeg or via Dubrava, that I have already mentioned. Sometimes it took an hour and a half, sometimes it took two hours, sometimes even longer than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to ask maybe to actually show by pointers the other routes that were used during the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, you can see that there is a local road from Neum via Stolac, all the way to Mostar, which is not on this map, and that is another route one can take from Neum to Mostar. Currently, what you do is you go from Neum to Opuzen, along the Neretva towards Mostar. During the war, we used alternative routes from Neum crossing the border of the Republic of Croatia via Metkovic. I can't see it here on the map. There it is. Then via Citluk, Ljubuski and Citluk. And then you can go further towards Mostar. I can see a road here. And then you could also take a road from Ljubuski via Grude which I don't see on this map and Siroki Brijeg again all the way to Mostar. Those were the routes that were used during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree with me that according to the 1991 census, there were approximately 4.325 people living in the municipality, that is the opstina, of Neum? Does that sound about right to you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is approximately the correct figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And out of that approximately 4.325 people, there were 3.792 Croats and in the entire municipality, 190 Muslims; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, how many Muslims --

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were about -- the number of Croats was more or less the same, as you mentioned. The reminders were Serbs, Muslims and the so-called Yugoslavs. A total number of others than Croats was about 12 to 13 per cent. So your allegation is not correct that there were only Muslims residing in the territory of Neum municipality together with Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That wasn't my question, sir. So let me restate my question and perhaps you'll listen to my question and answer my question. I didn't ask you how many Serbs there were. Is it correct, sir, that in the municipality of Neum, there were approximately 190 Muslims?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is approximately the figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you lived, sir, between October, 1992, approximately and February, 1994, and just so you're not wondering, I just simply picked those dates as the most relevant time period to the case.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you approximately. I can tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout this period, I lived in Neum with my family, and my family for ten days in 199-- ten -- [as interpreted] was outside Neum. That was in the month of May. And the rest of the time, both me and my family were in Neum. But I was very often absent, away on business, and I was engaged in the duties that I have already told you about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Where was your office or principal place of work located again during this approximate same time period from the latter part of 1992 until early 1994?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I have the transcript on the screen, please? Can you please repeat your question? Because I did not have the transcript on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Certainly. Where did you work, where was your office primarily located during that statement period from late 1992 to early 1994?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the end of 1992, at the beginning of 1993, I was mostly in Neum, together with my office, and later on, at the end of 1993, beginning of 1994, I was in Mostar. But during this specific period, I was very often away on business all over Herzegovina and even further than that, wherever there were passable routes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when you say during there time period you were engaged in business, are you talking about your vocational work, in terms of the way you'd made your living during most of your adult life or are you talking about work as a political official of either the HDZ party or the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I lived mostly and I was mostly engaged in politics in Neum, in Mostar and I had -- I worked in Neum municipality, in the HDZ of Bosnia and Herzegovina and in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, later on the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me come at it perhaps a bit differently. Can you tell the Chamber please again during this period from approximately October of 1992 to February, 1994, how often or how many times during that period were you personally in the city of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Mostar very often, sometimes every day, sometimes once a week. Depending on the requirements of my job. At the end of 1994, actually the end of 1993, beginning of 1994, I was there every day. When I took over the Office of the President of the Chamber of representatives of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, well up until the time you say you essentially at least for work purposes moved there to take the position you just described, before that time, can you give us some percentage of your time -- and we understand it will be an approximation -- of how much of your time you spent in Mostar as opposed to how much you were in Neum?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very difficult for me to say how much time. Sometimes I would even spend the night, either in Mostar or in Citluk or in some other places. Sometimes I would be in Mostar for a day or two. Sometimes I would be in Mostar just during the regular working hours, that is eight hours. And it all depended on the requirement of the job and the situation on the ground. Because at the time, sometimes we would work around the clock, 24 hours a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell me, sir, tell the Judges, how many times during that -- this same period were you in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult for me to say the exact number but I was in Siroki Brijeg several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, several times mean four or five times or 50 times?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this period, I am -- I was not four or five times but more. It was several dozens of times, 30, 40, but definitely I was more than four or five times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what business took you to Siroki Brijeg? What would you do there?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you were listening carefully to what I said during the examination, you could hear that in the area of Bosnia and Herzegovina, later on in the organised area of the Croatian Community Herceg-Bosna, that we had several various meetings, various discussions, and I was mostly in -- engaged in legislative activities and it is not difficult to imagine what business took me there. I had discussions with my associates about various positions that we were to hold, and here I am referring to the representatives, the leading figures, in Siroki Brijeg municipality and the general area of that municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Identify those persons, please.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Siroki Brijeg, I mostly communicated with Andjelko Mikulic and Mr. Jago Lasic, my associates at the level of Neum municipality. And later on I also met with Mr. Cosic and Mr. Mariofil Ljubic, who where representatives in the Chamber of Municipalities or in the Chamber of Citizens in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina while that republic functioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You're talking now specifically about 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 1993, the end of 1992, the period that we have been referring to from the very outset.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And sir, if I say these names incorrectly forgive me because I'm only referring to what's been put in the transcript. This man you mentioned and again reading from the transcript, I believe it will be Andjelko Mikulic, what was his position?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Andjelko Mikulic was the president of the municipal assembly of Neum, later on, the President of the Croatian Defence -- sorry, sorry, it was Siroki Brijeg municipality. And later on, the President of the Crisis Staff, i.e., the Croatian Defence Council for Siroki Brijeg municipality. Otherwise, he is an artist who did drawings, who did sculptures.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell the Chamber, please, during this same period of time, again approximately late 1992 to early 1994, did you ever have occasion to be in the vicinity of the villages of Sovici and Doljani?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sovici and Doljani are not in the area that we are now referring to. Sovici and Doljani are a bit more towards the north, and in this period of time, I was never in that particular area, the area of Sovici and Doljani, which belonged to Jablanica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges, sir, please, how many meetings of the HVO Main Staff did you attend during that period?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting -- I mostly did not attend the meetings of HVO Main Staff because this was not my duty, and I don't remember having attended any of the meetings of the Main Staff of the HVO during that particular period of time. I repeat, I had -- I worked in municipality of Neum and in the legislative power of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, later on the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you, in 1993, sir, have any military role? On behalf of the Bosnian Croat side?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, we did not get your question. Would you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, during this same time that we have been talking about, did you have any military role on behalf of the -- or in connection with the Bosnian Croat forces?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to warn you that personally I'm not an a Bosnian Croat and in Bosnia and Herzegovina, we are not Bosnian Croats. Please use the term which is official and that is a Croat from Bosnia and Herzegovina or Croats from Bosnia and Herzegovina, and during this period of time, I was a politician, I did not have any military position or post, because I had my office in Neum, i.e. I was a member of the legislative power of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges, please, did you attend any meetings involving the senior officers or commanders of an HVO or military unit called the Convicts Battalion during that time?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not attend any such meetings because this was not part of my duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, at any time during 1993, did you meet any officer of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not meet any officer, and I don't know -- I was not -- I did not attend any meetings and I did not meet with any persons belonging to this unit. I don't even know that it existed. I heard that it had, and that it was a unit under the command of Mr. Ivan Andabak, but personally, I did not have any meetings with them or any knowledge about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it fair to conclude from all this that the Judges should understand then that you have no knowledge of the Convicts Battalion, its activities or its officers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You're right. You're well informed. I do not have personal knowledge about this issue, the issue that you have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, in reference to the municipality of Neum, which we had before us on the map a few minutes ago, can you tell the Judges, please, at any time between late 1992 and early 1994, was there any fighting in that municipality between forces associated with the HVO or the HDZ and forces associated with the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that period of time, in the area of Neum municipality, there were -- just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know whether I have maybe misunderstood. The Prosecutor's said forces -- HDZ forces. What forces are these? This is the first time for 11 months of this trial. What are the HDZ forces?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, the reason --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, the reason I used that terminology was to avoid, in part, using the term Bosnian Croat. So simply if we can agree, I don't know if the witness believes there is were other forces besides the HVO, and I don't want to play word games with him, frankly, so I'm simply asking him forces associated with or part of either the HVO or the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is exactly what the -- my learned friend is doing. He's playing games. The witness has objected to me saying something like that, and then he asked the Prosecutor that when he refers to Croats who were citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that he should refer to them as Croats from Bosnia and Herzegovina, rather than Bosnian Croats, because such people do not exist. So what has that got to do with anything with HDZ?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I submit to you the witness knows exactly what I'm asking and he can answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think before that we should --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... which terminology, which words do you prefer, Croats in the -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not me. This is not me. I don't have a problem with anything but the Prosecutor, I already have experience from his previous cross-examinations, that he likes to play games.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to that completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already proven that, Your Honours. I have proven that to you during the cross-examination of Mr. Praljak. Now again, you're playing games with the HDZ forces, you're confusing the witness and nobody knows what this refers to. The witness told you clearly, loud and clear, that Croats in Bosnia and Herzegovina are Croats from Bosnia and Herzegovina, there are no Bosnian Serbs or Bosnian Croats. That's very simple. What seems to be the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scots, try another terminology that the witness could accept.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, let's see if we can come to agreement on terms that we can use for the remainder of your examination? There were organised armed forces that fought for the HVO, correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct. I would like to ask you and warn both you and the Court and all the present here that I personally, and all Croats in Bosnia and Herzegovina, should be referred to as is official and the way we feel. And that's "Croats from Bosnia and Herzegovina." And Mr. Prosecutor, there were no armed forces of HDZ. There was the Croatian Defence Council and there was the legal civilian police with its duties. There were no other forces in this area. I don't know what you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Perhaps, sir, --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, the Prosecutor asked you a question whether there are organised armed forces that fought for the HVO. And you said it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The Croatian Defence Council existed and it was the armed component of Croats in Bosnia and Herzegovina and Muslims while they were together. There were no other forces, just to clarify the matters, if there is a need for clarification. Sir, Mr. Prosecutor, if you need any further clarification, let's clarify things.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think we have established we can use the term HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I use the term HVO, sir, are you going to take that as the armed forces of what was then described as the Croatian community or later Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna? Can we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only armed component of Croats in Bosnia and Herzegovina throughout the period was the Croatian Defence Council. Let's use this terminology and things will be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. So during the period from late 1992 to early 1994, was there any fighting in the municipality of Neum between the HVO and the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?
